name: EI13 directed-square side-spindle conversion
source: Exoo--Ismailescu arXiv:1805.06055v1, Theorem 3.1 explicit second proof
coordinates: Exact in Q(sqrt(3),sqrt(7),sqrt(11))^2; source coordinates per paper.
square_rule: For every source distance-sqrt(2) pair A,B with source index A<B, add C=(A+B)/2+i(B-A)/2 and D=(A+B)/2-i(B-A)/2. Use directed sides A->D,D->B,B->C,C->A (counterclockwise).
unit_rule: Also use every original source unit pair A->B with source index A<B. Retain the multiset of 20+4*14 directed sides; collision merge only final coordinates.
spindle_rule: For directed unit side A->B put v=B-A, H=(A+B)/2-i*sqrt(11)*v/2. For X=A,B add H and both (H+X)/2 +/- i*(H-X)/(2*sqrt(3)). Together with A,B these seven points form a Moser spindle.
rationale: The source needs a fifth colour when all 14 diagonal inequalities are present. Every associated square side is placed in a four-chromatic spindle. Only nonseparable physical contacts in the global merged assembly could turn this into a strict unit-distance conversion; no inequality-forcing claim is assumed for an isolated spindle or square.
decision: Reconstruct every unordered physical pair and decide ordinary four-colourability on those exact graph bytes. If SAT, independently check literal word and retire source/architecture. If UNSAT, check proper five-word and independent refutation.
stops: need for another frame, handedness, carrier or gadget sweep
